title: GISS: Same-Goal Geometry Interventions for Strategy-Switch Generalization
hook: A policy can retain strong ordinary new-object success yet show a larger topology-conditioned success gap exactly when geometry makes its nominal strategy infeasible, even though the instruction, start distribution, and terminal 6D goal are unchanged. GISS turns that hidden split into an executable simulator diagnostic rather than another object-generalization leaderboard.
hook_shape_rationale: This is a surprising empirical reveal: the named topology-conditioned success gap is predicted to increase on compiler-certified strategy-switch pairs while aggregate endpoint success can conceal the split. A structural-reframe hook around endpoint-success sufficiency was viable, but rejected because the controlled metric direction is the stronger admission test and does not imply that prior papers explicitly made a causal claim they did not name.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved frontier leaf establishes causal identifiability for geometry-sensitive strategy generalization: under matched instruction, start distribution, and terminal goal, it remains unresolved whether policy behavior changes specifically because the original relation-event sequence or path class becomes infeasible 鈥?stakes: practitioners cannot tell whether a model will select a valid grasp, reorientation, approach, or insertion strategy on a geometry-altered deployment, and the field may attribute endpoint robustness to functional-geometric reasoning that was never isolated.
gap_closure.how_closed: C02 supplies compiler-certified matched geometry pairs and an evaluand-independent simulator oracle; the companion uses their switch-versus-nonswitch success divergence to audit the inherited endpoint-success assumption. Corpus support is thin in co-adaptive VLA/WAM manipulation, so the claim is scoped to the compiled RoboTwin 2.0 task families rather than general robot geometry reasoning.

core_mechanism: GISS adds a total task compiler to a scoped set of existing RoboTwin 2.0 manipulation families: for every requested family f, geometry vector g, and reset seed u, the compiler returns one of certified_switch, certified_nonswitch, infeasible, or uncertified rather than silently dropping a case. It holds the language instruction I_f, reset seed u, non-geometry simulator state, and terminal object 6D transform G_f fixed, and changes only the target or reference collision geometry. From SAPIEN contact, collision, attachment, and signed-region predicates, it converts every feasible expert execution into a reduced relation-event word w and couples that word to the collision-free path component returned by the family's finite strategy grammar; this simulator-derived pair is the strategy signature sigma, with no natural-language phase strings. The source-geometry signature sigma_0 is feasible by construction, and the switch bit q(g)=1 only when exhaustive checking within the declared finite grammar makes sigma_0 infeasible while at least one different signature is feasible; q(g)=0 marks a matched edit of nearest normalized geometry distance for which sigma_0 remains feasible. The grammar and its coverage are part of the benchmark specification, so the certificate is explicitly relative to that finite family and is not claimed to enumerate every manipulation strategy in nature. Pair records expose only ordinary RGB observations, proprioception, I_f, and G_f to OpenPI pi0.5, the released CLOVER checkpoint, and non-oracle comparators; sigma and q remain evaluator-side labels. For a policy P, the topology-conditioned success gap is TCSG(P)=E[S(P)|q=0]-E[S(P)|q=1] over compiler-certified matched pairs, where S is the native RoboTwin task-success predicate, and the invalid-old-strategy commitment rate is the fraction of q=1 rollouts whose simulator event prefix enters sigma_0 before failure. An Oracle-Graph adapter that receives sigma is reported only as an upper-bound headroom control, never as evidence that the ordinary-input policy inferred the graph. The companion audit overturns endpoint success as sufficient evidence only if TCSG and invalid commitment expose a switch-specific failure that survives realistic RoboTwin rendering and the Oracle-Graph control confirms usable strategy information. TCSG and commitment are diagnostic outputs; Oracle-Graph and any other trained adapter are privileged-information adaptation/headroom experiments only and cannot establish causal isolation or ordinary-input strategy inference.
core_mechanism_reasoning:
BLOCK 1 - PREMISES LEDGER
P1. RoboTwin 2.0 contains manipulation families whose collision geometry can be edited while preserving instruction, reset seed, and terminal object transform; its executable simulator and manipulation-relevant object annotations make this plausible, but whether the chosen families yield enough certified switches is untested - falsification target.
P2. Within each declared finite task grammar, SAPIEN collision/contact/attachment predicates distinguish task-relevant strategy signatures rather than merely superficial trajectory variation; untested - falsification target.
P3. A policy that represents functional geometry should lose less native success on q=1 than endpoint-only or PointMap-only comparators and should avoid early commitment to sigma_0; untested - falsification target.
OBSERVATION-MODEL. Geometry requests are sampled from preregistered bounded parameter ranges, but the estimand conditions on compiler-certified pairs, so it is not an unbiased estimate over all possible object geometries; policies receive only their standard RGB/proprioception/instruction inputs, while simulator state is reserved for compilation and scoring.
ESTIMAND. For each evaluated policy, TCSG is the paired average native-success contrast between nearest-geometry-distance certified nonswitch and switch edits under the same task family and reset seed; the secondary estimand is invalid-old-strategy commitment probability over the same certified q=1 population.
BLOCK 2 - NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT
The runnable naive version is to randomize object meshes in RoboTwin 2.0 and compare aggregate endpoint success across the resulting instances. Branch (i): it falsely assumes those randomized instances differ only in the need for a strategy switch, although broad geometry edits also change visibility, clearance, difficulty, and whether the nominal strategy remains feasible; GISS confronts that failure with same-seed matched edits, an explicit switch bit, and an independent simulator certificate. STANDARD-TOOL FOLLOW-UP: matched experimental design is textbook, but here the treatment is coupled to feasibility topology, the oracle must be generated from contact/collision dynamics without becoming a policy input, and controls must separate terminal-pose, generic PointMap, and oracle-graph headroom.
BLOCK 3 - DESIGN RATIONALE
The anchor and companion use the same matched-pair object: C02 constructs it and the assumption audit reads its measured split, so a second module or sibling gap would duplicate the contribution. Generic PointMap injection, tactile feedback, fixed language phase scaffolds, TAMP as the evaluated controller, and visual replanning were rejected because each occupies a lineage node or changes the question from diagnosing learned functional-geometry generalization. FULLTEXT WARNING: fulltext_degraded is true; all literature deltas below are explicitly abstract-level and must be rechecked before strong novelty claims.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Select a scoped set of existing RoboTwin 2.0 task families with editable target/reference collision meshes; register each family's fixed instruction, native success predicate, reset-seed distribution, terminal object transform, geometry parameter bounds, and finite strategy grammar as compiler inputs.
2. Implement the total GISS compiler in SAPIEN so every (f,g,u) request returns certified_switch, certified_nonswitch, infeasible, or uncertified plus a reason; do not filter failed planner calls without recording their status.
3. For each source geometry, execute the existing RoboTwin expert, convert simulator contact, collision, attachment, and signed-region transitions into w, and combine w with the grammar's collision-free path component to produce sigma_0.
4. For each geometry edit at the same reset seed and terminal transform, exhaustively check every candidate in the declared finite grammar using SAPIEN collision queries and executable rollouts; emit q=1 only when sigma_0 is infeasible and a distinct successful signature exists, and emit q=0 for the nearest normalized-distance edit retaining sigma_0.
5. Package certified switch/nonswitch records as the modest GISS-Pairs artifact with RGB, proprioception, instruction, native success, compiler status, and evaluator-side event traces; never expose q or sigma in the ordinary policy observation.
6. Run frozen OpenPI pi0.5 and the released CLOVER checkpoint on the identical paired resets, then score native success, TCSG, and invalid-old-strategy commitment from simulator traces.
7. Run equal-budget terminal-6D-pose, PointMap-only, and ordinary new-instance comparators on the same records; their action outputs propagate through the same simulator and are scored only by the same native predicate and evaluator-side event parser.
8. Train a small Oracle-Graph adapter on the same policy backbone with sigma as an upper-bound-only conditioning input, and run a label-permuted-sigma control; keep both separate from claims about ordinary-input generalization.
9. Report pair-level bootstrap intervals by task family and transfer the diagnostic to held-out RoboTwin object instances rendered with the platform's ordinary domain randomization; scope every claim to families where the compiler returned certified coverage. For every learned comparator or adapter comparison, preregister and match the base checkpoint, demonstrations, trainable-parameter budget, optimizer, update count, and seeds, and report frozen-policy diagnostics separately from trained-adaptation results.
falsification_prediction: Compile GISS-Pairs on existing RoboTwin 2.0 families and run matched seeds for frozen OpenPI pi0.5, the released CLOVER checkpoint, a terminal-6D-pose comparator, a PointMap-only comparator, and the Oracle-Graph upper bound. If the diagnostic reveals functional-geometry failure, native-success TCSG and invalid-old-strategy commitment increase on q=1 pairs despite fixed instructions and goals. The one load-bearing variable is the compiler-certified switch bit q; permuting q within task family and geometry-distance strata must collapse the native-success TCSG, while the unpermuted Oracle-Graph adapter must improve native success specifically on q=1. The idea is killed if terminal 6D pose or PointMap alone matches the Oracle-Graph switch-pair success, or if oracle event structure fails to improve native switch-pair success, because then the benchmark does not isolate useful strategy topology.
compute_budget: 36 GPU-days on 80GB-class A100 GPUs, at most 4 concurrent, covering compiler rollouts, matched evaluation seeds, lightweight Oracle-Graph adapters, controls, and the modest GISS-Pairs artifact; comfortable within the stated one-cycle envelope. $0 paid API: RoboTwin 2.0, SAPIEN, OpenPI pi0.5, CLOVER, compilation, and scoring use released code/checkpoints or local simulation.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: Abstract-only inference: RoboTwin 2.0 randomizes clutter, lighting, background, height, and language, whereas GISS constructs same-seed same-goal geometry pairs with an executable certificate that the nominal strategy becomes infeasible.

Abstract-only inference: GemBench spans placements, objects, primitives, and long horizons, whereas GISS measures a paired native-success contrast conditioned on whether geometry alone changes the feasible strategy signature.

Abstract-only inference: CoA-VLA supplies a fixed object/grasp/spatial/movement affordance chain, whereas GISS derives evaluator-side relation-event words from simulator transitions and tests whether their required topology changes.

Abstract-only inference: Any3D-VLA tests robustness from fused point-cloud representations, whereas GISS asks whether a PointMap-only policy closes the certified switch-pair gap relative to an oracle strategy graph.
Abstract-only inference: CLOVER replans from visual prediction error, whereas GISS separates recovery within a nominal plan from geometry-induced infeasibility of that plan's event/path class.

what_step_was_missed: RoboTwin 2.0 would have needed a total paired-geometry compiler that holds instruction, reset seed, non-geometry state, and terminal transform fixed, then certifies nominal-strategy infeasibility and an alternative simulator-grounded event/path signature before scoring policies by switch status.
